docs.title: AlphaFloor EFB User Guide
docs.text:
Welcome to the AlphaFloor EFB user guide. AlphaFloor EFB is an Electronic Flight Bag designed for ToLiss aircrafts in X-Plane 12. It provides complete operational flight planning, performance calculations, aircraft weight and balance management, charts, checklists, and ground servicing tools.

AlphaFloor EFB can be operated directly inside the 3D cockpit tablet or streamed over your local network to any tablet, iPad, phone, or computer.

docs.title: Supported Fleet
docs.text:
AlphaFloor EFB is optimized for the following aircraft in X-Plane 12:

  • ToLiss A319
  • ToLiss A320
  • ToLiss A320neo
  • ToLiss A321
  • ToLiss A321neo & A321XLR
  • ToLiss A330-900
  • ToLiss A340-600

docs.title: Operating Modes
docs.text:
1. 3D Virtual Cockpit Tablet: Replaces the default ToLiss EFB by default. It can be toggled on and off using the plugin menu in X-Plane's menu bar.
  2. External Device (Wi-Fi LAN): Connect your iPad, Android tablet, phone, or secondary computer to the same local network as your simulation PC. Open the network address displayed in the EFB Settings to control the EFB.

docs.title: Quick Navigation
docs.text:
• Installation Guide: How to install and verify the plugin.
  • Licensing & Free Trial: Starting your 7-day free trial, purchasing a lifetime license, and multi-device activation.
  • Interface & Controls: Cockpit interaction and remote web access.
  • Applications Guide: Step-by-step instructions for each built-in EFB application.
  • Troubleshooting: Solutions for common setup and network issues.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
This guide walks you through installing AlphaFloor EFB into X-Plane 12, verifying the setup, and configuring external tablet connections over your local network.

[!NOTE] The AviTab plugin should be disabled when using AlphaFloor EFB to avoid any unexpected interactions.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
• Flight Simulator: X-Plane 12 (version 12.00 or later).
  • Operating System:
  • Windows: Windows 10 or Windows 11 (64-bit).
  • macOS: macOS Monterey (12.0) or newer (Universal binary natively supporting Apple Silicon and Intel).
  • Linux: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Debian 12, Fedora 38 or equivalent 64-bit distribution with standard glibc.
  • Supported Aircraft: Any of the supported ToLiss Airbus models installed in your X-Plane 12/Aircraft/ directory.

docs.title: 1. Download the Release Archive
docs.text: Download the latest release archive (AlphaFloorEFB-vX.Y.Z.zip) from the CyberPatate Website.

docs.title: 2. Extract and Move to the Plugins Folder
docs.text:
Extract the downloaded .zip file. You will see a folder named AlphaFloorEFB.

Move the entire AlphaFloorEFB folder into your X-Plane 12 plugins directory:

X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/

Or use plugin management tools such as XLauncher.

docs.title: 3. Verify Folder Structure
docs.text:
Confirm that the folder hierarchy looks as follows:

X-Plane 12/
\-- Resources/
    \-- plugins/
        \-- AlphaFloorEFB/
            |-- mac_x64/
            |   \-- AlphaFloorEFB.xpl
            |-- win_x64/
            |   \-- AlphaFloorEFB.xpl
            |-- lin_x64/
            |   \-- AlphaFloorEFB.xpl
            |-- config.json
            |-- user_checklists.json.example
            |-- skunkcrafts_updater.cfg
            \-- user-guide.pdf

Important: Do not rename the AlphaFloorEFB folder. Keep all files in their respective subdirectories.

docs.title: First Launch & Verification
docs.text:
1. Launch X-Plane 12.
  2. From the flight setup menu, load any supported aircraft (e.g., ToLiss A320neo or A321).
  3. Once the 3D cockpit finishes loading, look at the tablet mounted beside the Captain's window.
  4. The tablet screen will power on and display the AlphaFloor EFB home screen.
  5. Click anywhere on the screen with your mouse to interact with the applications.

docs.title: Connecting External Devices (iPad, Android, Laptops)
docs.text:
You can use any external tablet, iPad, smartphone, or laptop as a standalone touch EFB while flying.

  1. Connect your external device to the same local Wi-Fi network as your flight simulator PC.
  2. In the 3D cockpit EFB, tap the Settings icon on the bottom navigation bar.
  3. Locate the Remote Tablet Access section. You will see an address such as: 
    http://192.168.1.42:40899
  4. Open your preferred web browser (e.g., Safari on iPad or Chrome on Android/PC) and enter that URL.
  5. The EFB interface will load with full touch functionality. Any action performed on the external device is instantly synchronized with the aircraft and the cockpit screen.

Tip for iPad users: In Safari, tap the Share button and select Add to Home Screen. This launches the EFB in full-screen mode without browser address bars.

[!NOTE] EFB remote access through a tablet is not compatible with the ToLiss Display App available with a Pro license.

docs.title: Updating AlphaFloor EFB
docs.text:
• Via SkunkCrafts Updater: AlphaFloor EFB includes full SkunkCrafts Updater integration. When an update is published, open your SkunkCrafts Updater client to download and apply the update. Your license file and custom checklists are automatically preserved.
  • Manual Update: Download the new .zip package from the website and overwrite the contents of X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/. Your license file (AlphaFloorEFB.lic or license.json) will remain intact.

docs.title: Screen Layout
docs.text: The tablet display is divided into three functional areas:

docs.title: 1. Top Status Bar
docs.text:
• Clock Display: Displays current simulation time.
  • Aircraft Type: Shows active aircraft variant (e.g., A319, A320neo, A321LR, A330-900, A340-600).
  • Power & Indicators: Visual indicators for battery charge level and network status.

docs.title: 2. Main Content Area
docs.text: This central viewport displays whichever application is currently open (e.g., Performance Calculator, SimBrief OFP, Charts, or Checklists).

docs.title: 3. Bottom Navigation Bar
docs.text:
• Home Button (Left): Instantly returns to the application launcher grid from any screen.
  • Quick Access Icons (Middle): Allows switching between the main applications without returning to the home screen.
  • Settings Button (Right): Opens the system configuration panel.

docs.title: In-Cockpit 3D Interaction
docs.text:
• Left Click: Tap any button, tab, input field, or checklist item.
  • Double Left Click: Quick zoom in/zoom out on documents and charts.
  • Mouse Drag: Hold the left mouse button and drag to scroll through documents, charts and list items.
  • Text Input: Click inside an input field (such as an airport ICAO code or gross weight) and type directly on your physical keyboard or use the virtual keyboard.
  • Minimizing to ToLiss ISCS: Click the Minimize icon in the top status bar to temporarily hide AlphaFloor EFB and interact directly with the native ToLiss ISCS screen (such as viewing faults or malfunctions). To restore AlphaFloor EFB, tap the native AviTab tab on the ToLiss tablet screen, execute the AlphaFloorEFB/toggle_overlay command, or toggle Enable EFB Overlay in the Plugins menu.

Important: "Use AviTab" must be selected in the ToLiss A/C + Sim Config tab to be able to switch back to AlphaFloor EFB by clicking on the AviTab tab.

docs.title: External Tablet & Mobile Interaction
docs.text:
When viewing the EFB on an iPad, Android tablet, phone, or laptop:

  • Tap: Equivalent to a mouse click.
  • Touch Drag: Smooth inertial scrolling through checklists, flight logs, and weather reports.
  • Pinch to Zoom: Zoom in and out of georeferenced airport diagrams and enroute charts.
  • Orientation Support: The interface automatically reorganizes its layout when switching between landscape and portrait orientations.
  • Full-Screen / Standalone Mode:
    • iPad / iOS: In Safari, tap the Share button and select Add to Home Screen. Launching AlphaFloor from the home screen icon runs it in standalone mode without Safari's address bar or navigation buttons.
    • Android / Desktop: Tap the Maximize / Fullscreen button in the top status bar (beside the battery indicator) or select Add to Home screen in your browser menu.

docs.title: Licensing & Free Trial
docs.text: AlphaFloor EFB offers a transparent, pilot-friendly licensing model. You can test every feature without restriction for seven days before deciding to purchase.

docs.title: 7-Day Free Trial
docs.text:
Every pilot is entitled to a 7-day free trial with full access to all applications and calculations.

  1. Launch X-Plane 12 with any supported Airbus aircraft.
  2. If this is your first time loading the plugin, the license prompt appears on the tablet.
  3. Click Start 7-Day Free Trial.
  4. Your trial period begins immediately. An indicator at the top of the Settings screen displays your remaining trial days.
  5. You do not need to provide a credit card, email address, or account registration to use the trial.

docs.title: Purchasing a License
docs.text:
When you are ready to purchase a permanent license:

  • Price: 11.99 € (single one-time payment, lifetime license).
  • In-app Purchase: Purchase the license directly from the EFB tablet within X-Plane 12.
  • Payment Processing: Processed securely through Stripe.
  • Updates Included: All minor and feature updates throughout the 1.x release cycle are included free of charge.

docs.title: Activating Your License
docs.text: After completing your purchase on the website, you will be redirected to an order confirmation screen. Your license is automatically validated in the EFB. You also have two alternative activation methods:

docs.title: Method 1: In-App License Key Entry
docs.text:
1. Copy the license key displayed on your confirmation screen (e.g., AFEFB-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX).
  2. In X-Plane 12, open the EFB tablet and tap the Settings icon.
  3. Select the License section.
  4. Paste or enter your key into the License Key field and click Activate.
  5. The status indicator will turn green and display Licensed (Full Version).

docs.title: Method 2: Standalone License File (AlphaFloorEFB.lic)
docs.text:
1. On your order confirmation screen, click the Download AlphaFloorEFB.lic button.
  2. Save the file directly into your plugin directory: 
    X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/AlphaFloorEFB.lic
  3. When you load the aircraft, AlphaFloor EFB automatically detects the file and activates your license without requiring manual key entry.

docs.title: Multi-Device Policy
docs.text:
• Up to 3 Personal Computers: Your purchase allows concurrent activation on up to three (3) personal computers (e.g., main flight sim desktop, laptop, secondary simulator rig) owned and operated by the same pilot.
  • External Tablets Do Not Consume Activations: iPads, Android tablets, phones, and laptops connected via local Wi-Fi to display the web interface are clients of your main simulator and do not count toward machine activations.

docs.title: Offline License Verification
docs.text: Once your license is verified, AlphaFloor EFB operates completely offline on your local computer.

docs.title: Refund Policy
docs.text: If you encounter technical defects or hardware incompatibilities that cannot be resolved within 14 calendar days of your purchase, contact support at contact@cyberpatate.fr for a prompt, full refund.

docs.title: Troubleshooting & FAQ
docs.text:
This section provides solutions for common setup questions, network connectivity, and troubleshooting tips.

[!NOTE] The AviTab plugin should be disabled when using AlphaFloor EFB to avoid any unexpected interactions.

docs.title: My iPad or tablet cannot open the EFB web page
docs.text:
• Same Wi-Fi Network: Ensure your mobile device and simulation computer are connected to the exact same Wi-Fi router or subnet. If your phone or tablet is connected to cellular 4G/5G or a guest Wi-Fi network with client isolation enabled, it cannot reach the PC.
  • Verify IP Address: Simulation PCs can change IP addresses if your router reboots. Check the Settings screen on the cockpit tablet to confirm the current IP address.
  • ToLiss Display App: EFB remote access through a tablet is not compatible with the ToLiss Display App available with a Pro license.

docs.title: My SimBrief flight plan does not load
docs.text:
• Confirm that your SimBrief Username or Pilot ID is entered correctly in the EFB Settings without extra spaces.
  • Ensure you have actively generated an Operational Flight Plan (OFP) on SimBrief.com before clicking Fetch.
  • Verify that your simulation computer has an active internet connection.

docs.title: Navigraph charts do not display
docs.text:
• Verify that your Navigraph account has an active Charts subscription.
  • Go to Settings -> Navigraph, tap Sign Out, and complete the authentication process again using the QR code or device code.

docs.title: My license key shows "Invalid Key"
docs.text:
• Ensure there are no accidental spaces before or after the key when copy-pasting.
  • License keys follow the format: key/XXXX.
  • If you purchased recently, ensure your payment was completed successfully on Stripe.

docs.title: Standalone file AlphaFloorEFB.lic is not detected
docs.text:
• Verify that the file is placed directly in the main plugin folder: 
    X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/AlphaFloorEFB.lic
  • Make sure your operating system has not appended an extra extension (such as AlphaFloorEFB.lic.txt).

docs.title: Contact Support
docs.text:
If you encounter an issue not covered in this guide, our support team is available to assist:

  • Support Email: contact@cyberpatate.fr
  • Website: https://cyberpatate.fr/alphafloorefb/

docs.title: Ground Services
docs.text: The Ground Services application allows pilots to manage aircraft doors, ground servicing equipment and external electrical power directly from the cockpit tablet.

docs.title: Doors & Hatches Management
docs.text: The application displays an interactive overhead schematic of the aircraft with real-time open/closed status for every door:

docs.title: Passenger Doors
docs.text:
• Door 1L: Main passenger boarding door (connected to jetway or boarding stairs).
  • Door 1R: Forward galley and catering service door.
  • Door 2L / 2R & 3L / 3R: Overwing emergency exits and mid-cabin doors (A321/A330/A340).
  • Door 4L / 4R: Aft passenger and service doors.

docs.title: Cargo Doors
docs.text:
• Forward Cargo Door: Opens the forward lower hold for luggage containers and pallets.
  • Aft Cargo Door: Opens the aft lower hold.
  • Bulk Cargo Door: Opens the rear bulk compartment.

docs.title: Quick Actions
docs.text:
• All Doors Open: Opens all doors simultaneously for rapid turnaround.
  • All Doors Closed: Closes and arms all doors prior to pushback.

docs.title: Ground Equipment Control
docs.text:
Toggle ground servicing objects when the aircraft is parked at the gate with engines shut down:

  • Wheel Chocks: Place or remove main gear chocks. (Ensure parking brake is set before removing chocks).
  • Ground Power Unit (GPU): Connects the ground power cart.
  • HP Air: Connects the high-pressure pneumatic air cart.
  • LP Air: Connects the low-pressure air conditioning cart.
  • Passenger Stairs: Summons front and rear boarding stairs for non-jetway stands.
  • Service Trucks: Drives catering scissor-lift trucks to galley service doors.

docs.title: Charts & Navigation
docs.text:
The Charts application displays aerodrome diagrams, departure routes (SID), terminal arrivals (STAR), and approach plates directly on the tablet screen with real-time aircraft position overlay.

Important Note: A Navigraph subscription is required for this application to work.

docs.title: Navigraph Account Linking
docs.text:
AlphaFloor EFB integrates directly with Navigraph Charts:

  1. Open the Charts or the Settings application on the EFB.
  2. If not previously signed in, tap Log in to Navigraph.
  3. A Navigraph login page is displayed. You can log in with your Navigraph credentials.
  4. The tablet will automatically refresh and connect to the worldwide Jeppesen chart database.

docs.title: 1. Pinned Airports
docs.text:
When a SimBrief flight plan is active, AlphaFloor EFB automatically pins your:

  • Departure Airport
  • Destination Airport
  • Enroute Alternate(s)

Tap any pinned airport badge at the top of the screen to view its chart directory.

docs.title: 2. Manual Airport Search
docs.text:
To search for any global airport:

  1. Tap the search bar in the top navigation header.
  2. Type the 4-letter ICAO code (e.g., EGLL, EDDF, KSFO).
  3. Press Enter to view all available charts.

docs.title: 3. Chart Categories
docs.text:
Charts are organized into standard operational tabs:

  • APT: Airport diagrams, parking stand charts, low-visibility taxi routes, and hot spot advisories.
  • DEP: Standard Instrument Departures.
  • ARR: Standard Terminal Arrival Routes.
  • APP: Instrument Approach Procedures (ILS, RNP, RNAV, VOR, Visual).
  • REF: Noise abatement, special departure procedures, and airport general notes.

docs.title: Interactive Chart Viewer Features
docs.text:
• Moving Map Position Overlay: On georeferenced taxi diagrams and approach plates, a magenta aircraft symbol indicates your exact real-time position and heading.
  • Day & Night Themes: Toggle between high-contrast daylight mode and dim night mode to preserve night cockpit vision.
  • Zoom & Pan Controls: Use your mouse click-drag in the cockpit, or natural pinch-to-zoom gestures on external tablets.
  • Rotation: Rotate landscape and portrait charts with the 90-degree rotate button.

docs.title: Moving Map & Georeferenced Enroute Overlay
docs.text: AlphaFloor EFB overlays your planned flight plan route and real-time simulator GPS telemetry onto a fluid, interactive navigation map:

docs.title: Checklists
docs.text: The Checklists application provides interactive normal checklists designed to streamline cockpit workflows and improve situational awareness.

docs.title: Standard Checklist Flow
docs.text:
AlphaFloor EFB includes the standard Airbus flight phase operational checklist flow:

  1. Cockpit Preparation
  2. Before Start
  3. After Start
  4. Taxi
  5. Line Up
  6. Approach
  7. Landing
  8. After Landing
  9. Parking
  10. Securing the Aircraft

docs.title: Operating Checklists
docs.text:
• Checking Items: Click or tap any checklist line item. The item highlights in green with a checkmark.
  • Phase Navigation: Use the left sidebar to jump between flight phases as your flight progresses.
  • Reset: Click Reset Phase to clear items in the active checklist, or Reset All to reset all phases for a new flight leg.

docs.title: Custom Checklists (user_checklists.json)
docs.text:
You can fully customize the checklists to match your airline's specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) or virtual airline requirements:

  1. Locate the example template in your plugin directory: 
    X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/user_checklists.json.example
  2. Make a copy of this file and rename it to: 
    user_checklists.json
  3. Open user_checklists.json in any text editor. It follows a clean, simple JSON format:
{
  "phases": [
    {
      "name": "Before Pushback",
      "items": [
        { "challenge": "Cockpit Prep", "response": "COMPLETED" },
        { "challenge": "Gear Pins & Covers", "response": "REMOVED" },
        { "challenge": "Signs", "response": "ON / AUTO" },
        { "challenge": "ADIRS", "response": "NAV" },
        { "challenge": "Fuel Quantity", "response": "____ KG BALANCED" },
        { "challenge": "TO Data", "response": "SET" },
        { "challenge": "Baro Ref", "response": "____ SET CROSSCHECKED" },
        { "challenge": "Windows & Doors", "response": "CLOSED" },
        { "challenge": "Beacon", "response": "ON" },
        { "challenge": "Thr Levers", "response": "IDLE" },
        { "challenge": "Parking Brake", "response": "AS RQRD" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
  1. Save your changes. AlphaFloor EFB will automatically load your custom checklist on next launch, preserving it across software updates.

docs.title: Documents Viewer
docs.text: The Documents application allows flight crews to view PDF flight documentation, Quick Reference Handbooks (QRH), airline Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and Flight Crew Operating Manuals (FCOM) directly on the tablet screen.

docs.title: Adding Your Own Documents
docs.text:
To make custom PDF documents available in the EFB:

  1. Navigate to one of the following folders:
  2. Your AlphaFloor EFB plugin folder: X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/documents/
  3. Per-aircraft folder: X-Plane 12/Aircraft/[aircraft_folder]/efb_docs/
  4. Create the folders if they don't exist
  5. Copy any standard .pdf files into the directory (e.g., A320_QRH.pdf, Company_SOP.pdf, Route_Briefing.pdf).
  6. Open or refresh the Documents application on the EFB. Your files will appear in the document library.

docs.title: Document Viewer Controls
docs.text:
• Document Library: Lists all available PDF, allowing to pin favorites for quick access.
  • Page Navigation:
  • Tap the Next Page and Previous Page arrows to flip pages.
  • Use the Page Jump box to type a specific page number and press Enter.
  • Zoom & Pan: Adjust reading scale using the Zoom In/Out controls. Pan using the mouse grab.

docs.title: Landing Performance Calculator
docs.text:
The Landing Performance application calculates landing distances, approach speeds, and stopping margins.

Prior to descent (during the arrival briefing):

  1. Select your destination or diversion airport and landing runway.
  2. Enter current runway surface conditions, barometric pressure (hPa or inHg), and reported winds.
  3. Confirm landing gross weight (in Tonnes or 1000 lbs according to your configured unit system in Settings). When syncing with SimBrief, estimated landing weights from LBS flight plans are converted automatically.
  4. Choose your desired flap configuration and braking method.
  5. Tap Compute.
  6. Review the resulting approach speeds, stopping distance, and runway remaining.

docs.title: 1. License Management
docs.text:
• License Status: Displays your current entitlement:
  • Licensed (Full Lifetime Version)
  • Active Free Trial (X days remaining)
  • Activate License: Input your purchased license key (key/XXXX) and click Activate.

docs.title: 2. Aircraft Unit System
docs.text:
• Unit System: Select your aircraft's unit system:
  • Metric (kg, m): Weights in Kilograms (kg) and Tonnes (t), barometric pressure in hPa.
  • Imperial (lbs, ft): Weights in Pounds (lbs) and 1000 lbs (klbs), barometric pressure in inHg.
  • This setting defines the default unit system used by the Performance and Weight & Balance applications.

docs.title: 3. Account Integrations
docs.text:
• SimBrief: Enter and save your SimBrief Pilot ID or username to automatically load dispatch flight plans.
  • Navigraph: View your Navigraph Charts connection status, authenticate, or sign out.

docs.title: 4. Charts Mode
docs.text: • Charts Mode: Toggle between dark and bright chart background.

docs.title: 5. Remote Access (Wi-Fi LAN Streaming)
docs.text:
• Server Status: Indicates whether the local network server is active.
  • Local LAN Address: Displays the exact URL to type into your external tablet or phone browser (e.g., http://192.168.1.42:40899).
  • Connection QR Code: Scan the QR code with your mobile camera to open the EFB interface without typing IP addresses.
  • Port Configuration: Change the default listening port (40899) if you have other software utilizing that port.

[!NOTE] EFB remote access through a tablet is not compatible with the ToLiss Display App available with a Pro license.

docs.title: 6. Synchronize EFBs
docs.text: • Synchronize EFBs: Enable or disable synchronization between all connected EFBs.

docs.title: SimBrief Operational Flight Plan (OFP)
docs.text: The SimBrief OFP application integrates with your SimBrief account to display your full operational flight plan, fuel calculations, route waypoints, and weather reports directly in the cockpit.

docs.title: Setting Up Your SimBrief Account
docs.text:
1. Open the SimBrief app from the EFB home screen (or navigate to Settings).
  2. Enter your SimBrief Username or numeric Pilot ID.
  3. Tap Save & Fetch.
  4. AlphaFloor EFB will query the SimBrief API and load your latest dispatch package. Your username is saved locally, so you only need to enter it once.

docs.title: 1. Flight Overview
docs.text:
Displays critical flight details at the top of the screen:

  • Flight Number & Call sign (e.g., AFR1234)
  • Departure & Arrival Airports with scheduled departure times and estimated flight duration
  • Alternate Airport(s) with distance and reserve fuel requirements
  • Cruising Altitude / Initial Flight Level (e.g., FL350)
  • Airframe Type & Registration

docs.title: 2. Fuel & Weight Breakdown
docs.text:
Summarizes planned fuel figures and weights for easy cross-checking with your MCDU. The app automatically detects and displays all quantities in either Kilograms (KGS) or Pounds (LBS) according to the units selected in your dispatch flight plan:

  • Block Fuel: Total fuel required on board before pushback.
  • Trip Fuel: Calculated burn for the planned route.
  • Contingency & Reserve Fuel: FAR/EASA regulatory reserves.
  • Alternate Fuel: Fuel required to divert to the planned alternate.
  • Zero Fuel Weight (ZFW): Planned aircraft empty weight plus payload.
  • Takeoff Weight (TOW): Calculated weight at brake release.

docs.title: 3. Route Navigation Log (Navlog)
docs.text:
Provides a scrollable navigation log listing:

  • Every airway, fix, and waypoint along the cleared routing.
  • Planned flight levels.
  • Forecast winds aloft (direction and speed).
  • Leg distance and estimated time.
  • Estimated Fuel On-board and editable Actual Fuel On-board entries to track fuel burn during flight.

docs.title: 4. Weather, METAR & TAF
docs.text:
Aggregates real-time weather reports for all airports along your itinerary:

  • Departure Weather: Raw METAR, decoded wind, altimeter setting (QNH/inHg), temperature, and runway surface reports.
  • Destination Weather: Current conditions and terminal aerodrome forecasts (TAF).
  • Enroute Alternates: Quick-reference weather cards for emergency diversion planning.

docs.title: 5. Full PDF Briefing Package
docs.text: View the complete, multi-page operational flight plan document formatted exactly as generated by your airline dispatch:

docs.title: Takeoff Performance Calculator
docs.text:
The Takeoff Performance application computes departure performance numbers for your flight.

To perform a takeoff calculation:

  1. Enter your departure airport and select the active runway.
  2. Verify atmospheric conditions (wind, temperature, barometric pressure in hPa or inHg).
  3. Confirm aircraft configuration (takeoff weight in Tonnes or 1000 lbs according to your configured unit system in Settings, packs, anti-ice).
  4. Tap Compute.
  5. Review the resulting FLEX temperature, V-speeds, and trim settings.
  6. Tap Insert in MCDU to transfer computed V-speeds (V1, VR, V2) and FLEX temperature directly into the aircraft FMGS.

[!NOTE] Due to ToLiss aircraft API limitations, the takeoff flap and pitch trim setting (FLAPS/THS, e.g. 1/UP0.5) cannot be inserted automatically via datarefs. You must enter this figure manually into line select key 3R on the MCDU PERF TAKEOFF page.

docs.title: Weight & Balance
docs.text:
To configure the aircraft payload and balance:

  1. Select your preferred unit system (KG or LBS) using the header toggle. The app automatically defaults to the system specified in your active SimBrief OFP, or the unit system configured in Settings if no OFP is active.
  2. Adjust passenger number and cabin distribution.
  3. Distribute freight across forward and aft cargo compartments (in kg or lbs).
  4. Set your required fuel quantity. When clicking Load SimBrief, planned fuel and cargo are automatically converted to kilograms before uplifting to the aircraft.
  5. Verify that the Center of Gravity (% MAC) remains within certified operational limits on the CG envelope chart.
  6. Tap Apply to Aircraft to synchronize values directly into the simulator.
